clue.text: Not entirely stupid about cooked fish — enough for a meal?

indicators.note: about means going round, so the shortened word wraps the rearranged one
not entirely means the word that follows loses its final letter

parts.note: dull means slow-witted

indicators.note: cooking transforms raw ingredients, so the following word is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone not quite dim cooks fish and wonders whether there is enough for supper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely stupid' reads as a description of the cook, but it means a word for stupid missing its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishful is the quantity a dish holds, which may or may not amount to a meal, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Father was first to swallow whiskey and took things slowly

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so the parent's word goes round the letter

parts.note: an informal word for father
whiskey is W in the NATO alphabet
being in front means having led

explanation.surface: Dad was quick to down a whiskey, then took it easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whiskey' looks like the drink, but it is the NATO code word for W.
explanation.definitionFit: To dawdle is to waste time or move idly, so dawdled matches took things slowly.

clue.text: Unable to proceed with wall preparation, something to cover damage

parts.note: stuck fast, not moving on
plaster is spread on walls before decorating

explanation.surface: A decorator stalls while plastering, trying to hide damage to the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: A sticking plaster is the British name for an adhesive bandage, like a Band-Aid; it also means a quick temporary fix.
explanation.definitionFit: An adhesive bandage covers a small wound, an injury to skin being a kind of damage.

clue.text: Statement of equality succeeded in markets

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the other word pair

parts.note: two fairs, a fair being a market
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, in family trees

explanation.surface: A claim that everyone was treated equally was borne out at the markets.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair's fair is a stock phrase insisting that something be divided or judged evenly.

clue.text: About to avoid bodies of water in African city

indicators.note: avoiding something means leaving it out, so a word for about is taken away

parts.note: lagoons are stretches of sheltered water
on as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: Someone steers clear of lakes in an African city.
explanation.walkthrough: LAGOONS loses ON from its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lagos is Nigeria's largest city, on the West African coast.

clue.text: Shouts pained comment, beset by alarms?

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded on all sides, so the outer word closes round the inner

parts.note: alarm bells
the cry someone makes when hurt

explanation.surface: A person lets out pained yells, surrounded by ringing alarms.
explanation.definitionFit: To bellow is to roar loudly, so bellows is a verb form meaning shouts.

clue.text: Work to accommodate patients — records shelved here?

parts.note: a book is a written work
a doctor calls patients cases

explanation.surface: A clinic works to fit in patients, with their files put away on shelves.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface also hints at booking cases in, as a receptionist schedules patients.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookcases are shelving units, so written records could be stored on them; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Reason officer's upset about American soldier

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the turned rank encloses the soldier
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the rank is read bottom to top

parts.note: Col is short for colonel; the 's is read as 'is'
a GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: An officer is upset about one of his American troops, for good reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic is reasoning, the process of thinking in an ordered way.

clue.text: Curious lad remade a virtue of popular choice

parts.note: odd means strange

indicators.note: something remade is rebuilt in another form, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: a son is a boy
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange boy turned virtue into a popular choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' belongs to the fodder rather than linking to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An odds-on favourite is the runner with the shortest odds, the one most backers choose.

clue.text: Bag made from piece of cloth, not wide but having a bit of extra length

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for wide is dropped

parts.note: a swatch is a fabric sample
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

indicators.note: a bit means just a small piece, here the opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter
L is the abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: A bag sewn from a fabric scrap is narrow but slightly longer.
explanation.walkthrough: W for wide is a cricket scoring abbreviation; 'not wide' asks for that letter to go.
explanation.definitionFit: A satchel is a shoulder bag, often used by schoolchildren to carry books.

clue.text: Working in restaurant, overlooked accommodating party for theatrical show

parts.note: waiting at tables

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to, so one word houses the other

parts.note: overlooked meaning neglected to remember
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A waiter forgot to look after a party booked in before a theatre show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overlooked' suggests a view, but it means neglected; 'for theatrical show' looks like a link, yet 'for' is the start of the second word of the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Waiting for Godot is Samuel Beckett's famous play, an example of a theatrical show.

clue.text: Return of marine creature, seen around 1,000 bodies of water

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the creature's name runs backwards
around means encircling, so the backward word surrounds the numeral's letter

parts.note: a seal is a sea mammal
K stands for a thousand, as in kilo

explanation.surface: A seal comes back to a scene with a thousand stretches of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Lakes are large inland stretches of water, so they are bodies of water.

clue.text: Dismiss clergy in sign of repentance?

parts.note: to sack is to fire from a job
the cloth is a collective term for the clergy

explanation.surface: Firing priests is presented as a kind of penance.
explanation.walkthrough: Wearing sackcloth and ashes is the biblical show of penitence.
explanation.definitionFit: Sackcloth was coarse fabric worn as a traditional outward mark of mourning or penitence.

clue.text: Overalls good — are needed in sandy areas

indicators.note: needed in places the first letters inside the area named

parts.note: dunes are sandy hills by the coast
G is the abbreviation for good
taken as written

explanation.surface: Good overalls are said to be essential on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are trousers with a bib and straps, a type of protective work garment.

clue.text: Doctor phoned in, having injected initially risky brain chemical

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the next word

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A doctor rang in after giving a risky injection affecting the brain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' poses as a noun but is the verb signalling the rearrangement; the R is added in before mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: Endorphins are hormones released in the brain and nervous system that relieve pain.

clue.text: Kidneys? Not eating a lot for starters

parts.note: off one's food means not eating

indicators.note: starters are the opening items, so only initial letters of those words count

parts.note: the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone is off kidneys, refusing to eat much of anything.
explanation.walkthrough: Offal is the edible innards of an animal; the question mark shows kidneys are just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidneys are internal organs eaten as food, an example of offal.

clue.text: Regulation formerly restricting racket amongst artillery

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the outer word confines what follows

parts.note: once means in the past

indicators.note: amongst means surrounded by, so the noise sits within the gunners

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: An old rule once limited the noise made by the gunners.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the noise sits among the gunners, and that pair sits within the word for formerly. RA is the Royal Artillery of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an authoritative rule or decree, such as a local by-law.

clue.text: Unduly active promoter?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: someone who hypes things up

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a playful coinage, hence the question mark: one who hypes is a hyper.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means overexcited; as a whimsical noun it names a person who publicises energetically.

clue.text: Power of France? Keep at a distance

parts.note: a hold over someone is power
taken as written
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: A question about French might, then an order to stay back.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold off an attacker is to prevent them coming near, repelling them.

clue.text: Flop around stone base in storm

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the failure's letters enclose the weight unit

parts.note: a dud is a failure
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight
base meaning morally low or wicked

explanation.surface: Something collapses around a stone foundation during a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like a foundation, but it is the adjective meaning wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: A dust devil is a small whirlwind carrying dust, a minor kind of storm.

clue.text: Italian course showing dip in road

indicators.note: in places the dip inside the word for road

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road
a sag is a dip

explanation.surface: An Italian road course shows a dip in its surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' suggests a racetrack but is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is a baked Italian pasta dish served as one course of a meal.

clue.text: Peers accepting article without borrowed terms

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the nobles' word holds the others

parts.note: peers of the realm are lords
the indefinite article
w/o is shorthand for without

explanation.surface: Lords take in a piece of writing without any other help.
explanation.definitionFit: Loanwords are terms one language adopts from another, so they are words borrowed.

clue.text: English force turning up in conflict — very thin rations?

indicators.note: in places the pair inside the word for conflict

parts.note: war is armed conflict

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means read from the bottom, so the pair is backwards

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
F is the symbol for force in physics

explanation.surface: An English army arrives in a war zone to find supplies very scant.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the phrase wafer-thin, and a communion wafer is a meagre portion.
explanation.definitionFit: A wafer is a very thin crisp biscuit, a slim helping of food.

clue.text: Drink including your medicine

indicators.note: including means taking inside, so the drinking word holds the possessive

parts.note: to sup is to sip
yr is the written abbreviation for your

explanation.surface: An instruction to drink up your medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A syrup is a sweet liquid used as a vehicle for doses of medicine, such as cough syrup.

clue.text: Sensible thinking about Northern contributions to language

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for common sense goes round the compass letter

parts.note: nous is practical intelligence
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: Clear thought about the north informs one's speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Nouns are naming words, one of the parts of speech that make up a language.

clue.text: Emerging from management not likely to succeed?

parts.note: coming out of
the running of a business is its management

explanation.surface: Someone stepping out of the boardroom is judged unlikely to make it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be out of the running is an idiom for having no chance of winning a contest.

clue.text: Language appropriate to tutor disregarding India

parts.note: suitable for

indicators.note: disregarding means leaving out, so the letter for the named code word is dropped

parts.note: to tutor is to train
India is I in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A language is described as suitable for teaching, if not in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'India' looks like a country, but it is the NATO code word for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortran is an early computer programming language, a crossword-friendly sense of language.

clue.text: Introduce piano and wind instrument keeping constant time at the end

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the instrument's letters hold the scientific symbol

parts.note: a reed is a woodwind instrument
c is the constant for the speed of light

indicators.note: at the end points to the final letter only of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A musician brings in the piano and a reed player who keeps steady time to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: REED holds C after its first two letters, and the final E comes from the end of 'time', not T for time.
explanation.definitionFit: To precede something is to come before it, as a preface or opening act may introduce what follows.
